data.narrative:
INTALUS, a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company led by Gene Skiba and Peter Ostlund, has raised $31M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 9 private peers (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Bedrock Robotics) and 1 public comparable, though meaningful peer-median triangulation was precluded by insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage datapoints within the narrow Robotics & Manufacturing segment.

Stage-progression methodology was the primary applicable approach, applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage transitions to the $31M raised proxy. This yields an implied valuation of $78M. Given the limited methodological basis, the analysis brackets this central estimate with a ±15% range: a low of $66M and a high of $89M.

The narrowness of this valuation rests on a single triangulation method. Key uncertainties include capital efficiency relative to the broader robotics cohort, INTALUS's specific technical differentiation within manufacturing automation, and burn rate trajectory through Series A. Peer-median analysis remains blocked pending visibility into same-stage or tier-matched valuation data. Updated comps or disclosed capital deployment metrics would sharpen conviction around the $78M median.
